speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Government will (i) study the doubling of paternity leave by several multinational companies in Singapore to examine the effect on employability, productivity and family relationships of the employees in these companies and (ii) consider doubling the paternity leave for all fathers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Paternity leave is also associated with stronger relationships between fathers and their children, as well as with their wives.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Government has progressively enhanced parental leave schemes to better support parents and, particularly fathers, in playing a bigger role in raising their children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, supporting the caregiving needs of parents must be balanced with the manpower and operational needs of employers, as I had explained in my Committee of Supply (COS) speech last week.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We welcome these progressive companies to share their experiences and best practices with other companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should first say we all welcome the Leader back to the House and we are glad she has recovered well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One is, I am just wondering whether the Government is going to review our parental leave policy, not immediately overnight, but, eventually, try to equalise it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I worry what message we are sending to our society when we say that mothers have 16 weeks of maternity leave and fathers have two weeks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Then, we are saying who is supposed to look after our children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In line with that, the second clarification is, there are studies now that show that our policies reinforce the gender stereotypes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I hope the Government can study some of these studies that are out there and also do additional studies to see whether our policies really do reinforce the gender stereotypes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would say that we agree that it is very important for fathers to be involved, especially at the early stage when the children are just born, for them to bond with the children and to be there for the wife and the family.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think the key adjustment that we need to make is a mindset change.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a mindset change partly on the part of fathers, partly on the part of employers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have found, for example, if we look at the statistics for the taking of parental leave, that there has been an improvement, but it is still not where we want it to be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You can see that it is improving, but it is not where we would like it to be.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The second part of the equation is also how the employers respond.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is very important because if someone applies for paternity leave and you find that the supervisor is not supportive or the colleagues are not willing to cover, it makes it very difficult for the father to take that paternity leave as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That mindset shift is something we are in transition because we see more fathers wanting to be involved; employers need to be on board.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Which is why both at COS and now, I am reiterating, as indeed Mr Ng is, that it is actually better for your organisation if you are family-friendly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is better for your organisation if you support fathers to take paternity leave, and, of course, mothers as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is something that we need to work with the tripartite partners on.
